text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Finance Minister Nasser al-Rodhan said the government has stopped withdrawing from the state's Future Generation Fund since October 1996, reimbursing it with $2 billion. The Fund, an overseas nest egg once estimated at about $100 billion, shrank to around $40 billion mainly due to the 1991 Gulf War costs.
- Kuwait to host on April 7 an Indian real estate and investment fair.
- Oil Minister Isa al-Mazeedi to attend an oil and gas conference in Iran in May.

- Information Minister Sheikh Saud Nasser al-Sabah flew to Qatar to protest against a television programme broadcast by the Doha-based al-Jazira satellite channel. Qatar told Sheikh Saud the state had no control on the channel's programmes.
- Kuwaiti officers complete an air defence course in the United States.

- MPs focus at Tuesday's parliament session on unemployment, the status of stateless people and narcotics. Some 100,000 stateless people, mainly Arabs, reside in Kuwait but are denied the freedom to travel abroad and benefit from some state services like higher eductaion.
- A 23-year-old Arab man arrested for allegedly kidnapping and raping a five-year-old boy on Sunday.
- Egypt hosts an open debate on Kuwait's prisoners of war. Kuwait says Iraq still holds some 600 Kuwaitis since the Gulf crisis.
